time_based_recommendations.morning: Wear layers and consider a light scarf or mask to protect against dew/pollen.
time_based_recommendations.afternoon: Avoid prolonged exposure in damp, shaded areas; seek shelter if wind gusts are strong.

time_based_recommendations.night: Keep windows closed and use dehumidifiers or air purifiers to manage indoor mold risk.

image_specific_alerts.identified_hazard: High ambient humidity (98%) combined with potential organic debris suggests a high risk of unseen mold/mildew growth.

botanical_and_weather_triggers.details: This level of humidity significantly increases the risk of mold and mildew growth in both natural and built environments, posing a respiratory threat.
The moderate wind speed, especially with gusts, will effectively transport pollen and spores over long distances, increasing exposure risk.
The sheer number of local plant species indicates a high potential for multi-allergen reactions, even if current air readings are low.

preventative_recommendations: Keep windows and doors closed during peak wind times to minimize spore/pollen entry.
Use HEPA air filters indoors, especially at night, to manage mold spores.
Wear a high-filtration mask (N95 or equivalent) if exercising outdoors on windy days.
Dress in layers of breathable, natural fabrics to combat wind chill and dampness.
Keep antihistamines and nasal saline spray readily available for immediate symptom relief.
